about.title: Downey Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: From the shops around Stonewood Center to apartment complexes, restaurants and parking structures across Downey, property owners have a legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe. When they ignore a spill, a cracked sidewalk, a loose handrail or poor lighting and someone gets hurt, California law may hold them responsible. These cases turn on proving the owner knew — or should have known — about the hazard and failed to fix it, which is why preserving evidence early matters so much. LawProactive connects injured Downey residents, at no cost, with an independent premises liability attorney. You pay no fee unless your case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: What makes a strong premises case

items.title: Report it and document it
items.desc: Ask for an incident report, photograph the hazard and your injuries, and keep the shoes and clothing you were wearing. This evidence often vanishes within a day of the fall.

items.title: The 'notice' question is everything
items.desc: You generally must show the owner knew or should have known about the danger. An attorney can subpoena maintenance logs and camera footage to establish it.

items.title: Two-year California deadline
items.desc: You typically have two years to file — and shorter deadlines apply if the property is owned by a city, county or other public entity.

items.question: What do I have to prove in a Downey slip and fall case?
items.answer: Generally that a dangerous condition existed, the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about it, they failed to fix or warn about it, and that failure caused your injury. Photos, incident reports and maintenance records are key.

items.question: The store says the fall was my fault. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly at fault — your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility, not eliminated.

items.question: How soon should I contact an attorney?
items.answer: As soon as possible. Surveillance video is often overwritten within days and hazards get repaired, so early action helps preserve the proof your claim depends on.
